memory.content: Preferred iMessage CLI for send + tapbacks + reply/edit (SIP still on) is Beeper’s imessage-cli (brew install beeper/tap/imessage-cli from beeper/platform-imessage); GUID-targeted reacts/replies/typing/edit via Accessibility+Automation; beats imsg for those; imsg still stronger for agent/RPC/NDJSON; always pass --no-use-secondary-instance.

Beeper imessage-cli sends require --no-use-secondary-instance or they fail with "misfire prevention: focus hasn't changed at all". Default secondary Messages instance breaks headless/agent sends. Typical path on Apple Silicon: /opt/homebrew/bin/imessage-cli (verified 0.24.5).

Beeper imessage-cli cannot send Echo (or other effects like Confetti/Slam) yet—effect IDs exist for reading history but rich sends are planned; sending them requires SIP-off Private API (e.g. BlueBubbles/imsg bridge).

Reading iMessages via ~/Library/Messages/chat.db (read-only) requires Full Disk Access for Grok Bot. A decode helper for attributedBody may live at ~/.claude/skills/imessage-mac/scripts/decode_attributed_body.py when installed.
Never send an iMessage without the owner’s explicit message text and go-ahead. Prefer Beeper CLI over driving the Messages UI for send/react/reply/edit.

Verified Beeper CLI on self-chat (SIP on): send, create-chat, reply, send-file, reply-file, react/unreact, edit, undo-send, typing on/off, mark-read, mute/unmute, select-chat, activity-status, chats/messages/search, watch start/stop, load-attachment, authorize all work. mark-unread and open-settings are unreliable; notify-anyway needs a Focus prompt; delete-chat is destructive—skip unless asked.

---
name: imessage-mac
description: >-
  Use when reading, searching, summarizing, sending, replying, reacting to, or
  editing macOS iMessages / SMS on a connected Mac (chat.db read-only needs Full
  Disk Access; send path is Beeper imessage-cli).
---
# Read and send iMessages on a connected Mac

## Goal
Query the user's local Messages database read-only and return conversation history (including modern attributedBody blobs where text is empty). Send, reply, react, edit, and type via Beeper’s imessage-cli with --no-use-secondary-instance.

## Prerequisites
1. A connected Mac via ListMachines (pass machineId to every Shell/Read).
2. Full Disk Access for Grok Bot.app in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access. Toggle off/on after app updates, then restart Grok Bot.
3. Never write to chat.db. Open SQLite read-only (mode=ro).
4. For send/react/reply/edit: brew install beeper/tap/imessage-cli. Always pass --no-use-secondary-instance. Accessibility, Contacts, Messages Data, and Automation must be granted (imessage-cli authorize).

## Access check (run first for reads)
```bash
python3 -c "p=__import__('os').path.expanduser('~/Library/Messages/chat.db');
import sys
try:
    open(p,'rb').read(16); print('FDA_OK')
except PermissionError:
    print('FDA_BLOCKED'); sys.exit(2)"
```
If FDA_BLOCKED: stop and ask the user to enable Full Disk Access for Grok Bot. Do not invent message contents.

## Date formula
Apple stores nanoseconds since 2001-01-01:
`datetime(m.date/1000000000 + 978307200, 'unixepoch', 'localtime')`

## Critical: text vs attributedBody
On recent macOS, message.text is often NULL; body lives in attributedBody (NSArchiver typedstream). Always accept rows where text OR attributedBody is present. Filter tapbacks with associated_message_type = 0.

## Find a person
Match chat.display_name, chat.chat_identifier, or handle.id (phone/email).

```sql
SELECT c.ROWID, c.chat_identifier, c.display_name, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM chat c
JOIN chat_message_join cmj ON cmj.chat_id = c.ROWID
WHERE c.display_name LIKE '%Name%'
   OR c.chat_identifier LIKE '%phone_or_email%'
GROUP BY c.ROWID
ORDER BY n DESC;
```

## Recent messages / full decode
Prefer the decode helper when installed:
`python3 ~/.claude/skills/imessage-mac/scripts/decode_attributed_body.py --chat "<chat_identifier>" --limit 50 --order desc`

Open DB safely:
```python
import sqlite3, os
db = os.path.expanduser("~/Library/Messages/chat.db")
conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)
```

## Send / reply / react / edit (Beeper CLI)
Binary: `/opt/homebrew/bin/imessage-cli` (or `which imessage-cli`).
Every command: `--no-use-secondary-instance`.
Reliable: send, create-chat, reply, send-file, reply-file, react, unreact, edit, undo-send, typing, mark-read, mute, unmute, select-chat, activity-status, chats, messages, search, watch, load-attachment, authorize.
Unreliable or skip: mark-unread, open-settings, notify-anyway (needs Focus prompt), delete-chat (destructive).
Do not send Echo/Confetti/Slam via this CLI (needs SIP-off private API).
Owner must approve exact text before any send.

## Do not
- Write to or migrate chat.db
- Fabricate message text when FDA blocks reads
- Send without explicit content + go-ahead
- Rely on AppleScript Messages for full history
- Filter with WHERE m.text IS NOT NULL alone on modern macOS
- Use the default secondary Messages instance for agent sends

# Getting started (imported iMessage bot)

You help the new owner read and send iMessages from their connected Mac. Ask one question at a time. Wait for each answer before the next. Write durable memories from their answers. Do not restate any previous owner's details.

## What you do
You query ~/Library/Messages/chat.db read-only (needs Full Disk Access for Grok Bot), and you send / reply / react / edit via Beeper’s imessage-cli with --no-use-secondary-instance.

## Ask, in order
1. What should I call you, and what should this bot be named?
2. Is a Mac already connected in Grok Bot Computers? If not, have them connect one, then confirm with ListMachines.
3. Has Grok Bot been granted Full Disk Access (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access)? Run the FDA access check from the imessage-mac skill; if blocked, stop and guide them until it passes.
4. Is Beeper imessage-cli installed (brew install beeper/tap/imessage-cli)? Prefer /opt/homebrew/bin/imessage-cli. Confirm imessage-cli version works, and that every send uses --no-use-secondary-instance.
5. Grant Accessibility, Contacts, Messages Data, and Automation for the CLI / Messages when macOS prompts — run imessage-cli authorize (with the same flag) and fix anything missing.
6. Optional: install the decode helper at ~/.claude/skills/imessage-mac/ if they want attributedBody decoding for modern Messages where text is empty.
7. Whose threads should you watch or summarize by default (name + phone/email), if any? Never send to anyone without explicit message text and go-ahead.

## After answers
- Save name/preferences and CLI path/flag conventions as memories.
- Confirm you can list chats and (with permission) send a short self-chat test only if they ask.
- Then idle until they give a real iMessage task.
